stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s price is hovering just 0.2% below its 52‑week high, reflecting a modest 1.1% daily gain and solid 26% YTD upside. The stock remains near the top of its range after an 8% monthly rally, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of sustained momentum.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft sits 2.8% shy of its 52‑week peak, having posted a modest 1.3% daily decline but a 6.3% gain over the month and 11.2% YTD. The next catalyst is the company’s cloud spending outlook, which will indicate whether the recent uptrend can be maintained.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA is trading 3.7% below its 52‑week high after a 2.9% drop on the day, though it’s still up 22% YTD. With the stock near the top of its range, investors should focus on the upcoming AI‑related product roadmap and inventory trends for direction.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet remains 13.4% off its 52‑week high, after a slight 0.6% dip but a 3% weekly gain and 10.7% YTD rise. Key watch points include the latest ad‑revenue data and progress on AI integration, which could push the stock back toward its highs.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon is 10.5% below its 52‑week high, posting a 2.3% daily decline but modest 0.7% monthly growth and 12.2% YTD gain. Investors should monitor retail traffic trends and cloud‑service earnings for clues on whether the stock can reclaim higher ground.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta trades 7.3% under its 52‑week high after a flat daily move and a 10.4% monthly surge, delivering an 11.1% YTD rise. The next focus is on user growth and monetization of its AI‑driven products, which could drive the stock back toward its peak.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla sits 23.5% below its 52‑week high, down 0.7% on the day but up 5.9% over the week, while remaining down 14.4% YTD. Investors should watch production updates and margin trends, especially given the sizable gap to its recent highs.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom is 25% off its 52‑week high after a 4.3% daily drop, though it’s up 4.2% YTD. The key metric to follow is its semiconductor demand outlook and any guidance on new chip launches, which could stabilize the price near its lows.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD trades just 4.4% below its 52‑week high, after a 3.9% daily decline but a spectacular 177.7% YTD gain and 19.1% monthly jump. The next watch point is the company’s product roadmap and competitive positioning in the GPU market, which will dictate whether the rally can continue.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 5.5% on the day and is down 30% YTD, trading 56.2% below its 52‑week high and 18% above its low, indicating a deep discount to recent peaks. The recent pullback follows weaker cloud guidance and macro pressure on enterprise spending. Investors should watch the upcoming earnings and any sign of renewed cloud order flow.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is modestly up 1.4% today but remains 13.8% off its 52‑week high while sitting 52% above its low, reflecting a still‑elevated valuation after a volatile year. The stock’s next catalyst is the Q4 results and progress on its AI‑driven product roadmap. Look for guidance on subscription renewals and AI adoption rates.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan is marginally higher today, up 0.6%, and sits 8.8% below its 52‑week high and 18.9% above its low, keeping it near the top of its range. The bank’s performance is tied to interest‑rate dynamics and loan growth. Watch the upcoming earnings for net interest margin trends and any shifts in credit quality.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America is flat to slightly up, trading 0.2% higher, still 16.9% below its 52‑week high and 15.9% above its low, indicating a mid‑range position. The stock’s trajectory will hinge on the Fed’s rate outlook and the bank’s deposit‑cost management. Key focus: the next earnings release and any updates on loan‑loss provisions.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is modestly stronger, up 0.8% and has risen 4.2% over the week, now only 2.4% shy of its 52‑week high while 27.4% above its low, suggesting near‑peak momentum. The next driver will be transaction volume trends amid consumer spending patterns. Investors should monitor quarterly volume guidance and any shifts in interchange fee dynamics.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard is up 0.8% and sits 4.2% below its 52‑week high, 22.1% above its low, maintaining solid upside in a high‑range environment. The key watch point is the upcoming earnings and the impact of emerging payment‑tech competition on fee growth. Look for updates on cross‑border volume and new product adoption.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix bounced 2.7% on the day and is 42.3% below its 52‑week high but only 6.7% above its low, indicating a steep discount yet limited downside left. The next catalyst is subscriber growth and content spend efficiency in the upcoming earnings. Watch for guidance on churn rates and the performance of the ad‑supported tier.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly slipped 1.6% but remains 8.6% below its 52‑week high and 47.2% above its low, holding near the top of its range after strong earnings. The upcoming driver is its pipeline progress and pricing trends for its diabetes and obesity drugs. Investors should focus on Q4 results and any FDA decisions affecting new launches.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth fell 1.3% but is still 14.5% below its 52‑week high and 44.9% above its low, trading in the upper‑mid range after solid YTD performance. The next inflection point is its earnings and updates on Medicare Advantage enrollment and cost‑containment measures. Watch for guidance on enrollment growth and medical cost trends.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has slipped 0.8% today and 4.0% over the month, sitting 7.9% below its 52‑week high but still 41.0% above its low, reflecting a modest pullback after a strong YTD gain of 25.7%. The recent dip appears tied to broader healthcare sector pressure rather than company‑specific news. Investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance and any developments in its pharmaceutical pipeline for direction.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart rose 2.2% on the day and is up 6.0% week‑to‑date, trading 17.4% under its 52‑week high while still 10.8% above its low, indicating resilience despite a slight YTD decline. The stock’s bounce aligns with solid retail traffic and pricing power. Key focus will be the next same‑store sales report and any updates on its e‑commerce initiatives.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco gained 0.6% today and is up 5.0% month‑to‑date, sitting 13.2% below its 52‑week peak but 12.0% above its trough, maintaining a healthy YTD rise of 11.4%. Membership renewals and inventory management continue to drive performance. Investors should monitor the upcoming quarterly earnings for clues on margin pressure from higher freight costs.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot jumped 3.4% on the day, though it’s down 12.7% YTD and sits 22.8% under its 52‑week high, only 5.1% above its low, suggesting a recent rebound after a broader discretionary slump. The lift follows strong DIY demand reports. Watch the next earnings release for guidance on inventory levels and consumer spending trends.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil rose 2.7% today, trading just 0.5% below its 52‑week high while up a massive 56.7% from its low, reflecting a robust YTD gain of 40.1%. The near‑record price underscores strong oil price momentum. Investors should keep an eye on crude price forecasts and the company’s capital‑allocation plan, especially dividend sustainability.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola advanced 2.3% on the day, now 4.0% under its 52‑week high and 35.8% above its low, with a solid YTD increase of 29.4%. The move follows positive pricing actions and steady demand. Key watch points include the upcoming earnings beat expectations and any shifts in global currency impacts on margins.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney climbed 2.2% today, sitting 6.9% below its 52‑week high and 16.7% above its low, after a modest YTD decline of 3.6%. The rally reflects optimism around its streaming subscriber growth and theme‑park recovery. Investors should focus on the next earnings report and any updates on content spend and park attendance trends.
